column3: The literal equality for every degree-at-most-one subset fails for U empty as n grows; the intended uniform upper bound is distinct. Do not earn credit from the missing inequality. The unsaturated upper-bound problem has no full route here.

All p,q and every dimension/multi-index are quantified. Finite pair-correlation tests cannot establish complete quasi-equidistribution; the correlation definition and irrational-base truncation rules need the primary body.

All forests of every n>=12 and uniqueness are required. A transfer recurrence for one branching tree would not prove global second extremality; the path-gluing convention also needs primary definitions.
The existential graph must work for each epsilon, with a minimal generating set. Generic high-chromatic Cayley graphs do not preserve minimality, so no full constructive mechanism is supplied.
Uniformity in dimension over every normalized log-concave measure is essential. One-dimensional or product inequalities are not a full log-Sobolev KLS bound.

Definition 4.3 and Conjecture A in the primary match unique minimal upper/maximal lower bounds for every pair. Finite posets cannot witness a failure; an infinite example must satisfy both uniqueness conditions globally. No such checked example is supplied; do not confuse minimal and least.

The displayed formula and status conflict; induced containment is critical. A non-induced bounded-degree tree embedding would not settle the intended range p~1/n through constant p, uniformly over trees.
The n=3 specialization already asks for a weak abc bound. Nonvanishing proper subsums and a bound uniform over all tuples prevent a finite certificate or a simple cancellation construction.
Pairwise coprimality eliminates the obvious cancelling large pairs, and n=3 again contains weak abc. No full bound in all tuple sizes is available.

Both a character-sum inequality for every finite group and the iff equality clause are required. Abelian orthogonality only checks the equality direction; small-group tables do not provide a uniform mechanism.

A gap in the finite determinant-root set needs a precise source definition of gap. Unconditional control for every even order cannot be inferred from a skew-conference construction conditional on existence.

Primary Conjecture 1.5 is explicitly confirmed there by Chen-Hao Theorem 1.6. Use k+1 parts of size at least k+2 to get threshold numbers 2k and 2k+1. Public theorem statement defeats a new brief; original Chen-Hao proof body and dependencies were not audited.
A linkage threshold alpha(k) independent of the matroid and the two circuits is required for every k. Checking graphic or regular matroids cannot supply the full arbitrary-matroid statement.
All d>3 and motivic identities, rather than numerical partition counts, are quantified. Interpolation without a proven coefficient constraint does not reduce the required new data to half.
Equality of word measures on every finite group must imply an automorphism for every free-group word. A finite list of test groups cannot certify the universal rigidity conclusion.

The inner-product display contains a subtraction transcription defect. After repairing to standard Orthogonal Vectors, the claim is an all-algorithm fine-grained lower bound, not a small constructive certificate.
The literal statement itself reports a 2005 Pach-Tardos refutation. No proof body was inspected, so do not upgrade to independently audited retirement; no rediscovery investment is justified.
Each tournament forest needs one exponent governing all n. A few small tournament embeddings do not control arbitrary forests or produce the polylogarithmic augmented-edge bound.

All planar H and unrestricted host graphs are quantified; bounded-degree induced-grid results do not bridge to this scope. The appended status quote has different parameters and cannot be treated as resolution evidence.
All subgraphs of every admissible cycle power must be Hamiltonian. Deleting a cut requires a degree certificate at every boundary vertex; no such full counterexample or constructive proof is in hand.
The vertex-dependent half-degree-plus-two threshold matters near path endpoints. A minimum-degree theorem or an interior-only cut construction does not establish or refute the full statement.
Forcing must determine the entire permuton; parameter counts or a finite density calculation alone cannot prove the universal lower bound six across unequal pattern sizes.
The C5 Cartesian powers already supply only the lower bound for every even degree. A larger positive-curvature graph needs an exact curvature verification on every edge, and no candidate is supplied.

The retained v1 HTML body has no kissing passage; selected sections concern planar packing and domains. Literal dimension/exponent claims must be matched to the correct source version before a kissing configuration is credited. No alternate-version fishing or numeric packing search was attempted.

The universal lower bound 2n for all digraph placement games requires the legal-move and value rules. An option-count lower bound needs proof that left/right options require distinct vertices; that bridge is not assumed.

Uniqueness ranges over all 12-subsets of the 30 cube types. A trustworthy exact certificate needs source cube orientations, assembly rules and a complete orbit reduction; none was substituted by tag-based screening.
The unresolved strip 2k+1<=n<2k+2d-3 requires a min-degree bound for every intersecting family. The known d<=2 or larger-n theorems do not settle all d.
All partitions into cycles of lengths at least three are required. The status quote is an oriented Hamilton-cycle theorem at a different threshold and cannot clear arbitrary directed cycle factors.
For each n the upper bound needs n-1 colors with every triangle multiset distinct. The palette count is only a necessary condition; no all-n edge-label construction is supplied.

A positive universal c and the dependence of sufficiently large n on r need primary precision. Literal c=0 would be a wording triviality and receives no credit. No linear lower-bound mechanism is supplied.

Existence of a quadratic-density limit for every ell requires a uniform extremal argument. Ordinary random vertex restriction normalizes by n cubed, not n squared; naive monotonicity does not establish the requested limit.

Conjecture 2 matches the primary. Corollaries 3.20-3.21 prove the claim for characteristic zero or characteristic at least k using (k-1)!; small characteristic is the obstruction. The paper already reports CoCoA checks through k<=5 over several small fields. Repeating those cases would not justify a new brief.

Primary Conjecture 1.3 exactly matches the record. Theorem 2.3 proves the stronger non-Hamiltonicity for every m<=4Delta-3 using the constructed tree T_Delta and a component-count obstruction. Selected proof body and Lemmas 2.1-2.2 were read; no full dependency or figure audit is claimed.

The leading lambda is not used consistently with the displayed k>t/3 threshold. Exact intended range needs source reconciliation; neither a quantifier repair nor a single clique-size instance earns full credit.

The role of D2 as maximum bipartite edges versus distance from bipartite must be checked in the primary, along with allowable zero-sized blowup parts. A trivial domination using a bipartite blowup could be a definition artifact, not the intended conjecture.

The parameter n in HB3 is insufficiently specified for an exhaustive word search. A deletion operation must preserve the exact hole/border constraint, not just word length; no full monotonicity mechanism is available.
Equality for all n compares four letters with arbitrary alphabet size. Finite optimal words or the related sparse-ruler analogy do not prove a universal alphabet-reduction map.

The distribution of T is not specified in the literal statement. Even with the intended random-tree law, concentration up to ell=o(sqrt(t)) requires more than the restricted-range estimate; no model-independent claim is made.
This is a uniform complexity dichotomy over fixed l, lambda and several backbone families. Individual reductions or trivial large-color regimes do not resolve every remaining parameter range.

All planar point sets and every choice of an EMST bipartition are quantified. Triangular chains certify tightness only; the missing approximation upper bound needs geometric control of both monochromatic trees.
A strict upper bound below two with probability tending to one is stronger than simulated ratios. No concentration argument controlling the maximizing bipartition is supplied.
One nearly linear function must work for every minor-closed family. Surface-specific bounds do not yield the universal oriented-clique/chromatic comparison without a structural theorem bridge.
Isolation and quadratic irrationality are required for every n. A prime-n algorithm conditional on termination is neither a termination proof nor a certificate for composite n.
The global maximum ranges over every prime p, not just a computed prefix. Verifying the value at 67 leaves the infinite comparison and termination obligations untouched.

Some positive crossing numbers have no knot with a reduced alternating diagram, so the literal minimum needs a source domain. Repairing that domain earns no credit; the intended all-crossing ascending-number lower bound remains substantial.

Both bipartiteness and the edge maximum-degree equality must hold at arbitrary diameter. The classified L<=5 cases supply instances only, and no curvature rigidity mechanism for general L is established.

The exact r-boundary is not defined in the record. Expected boundary versus alpha(H)^r times d n^(1-r) for every linear hypergraph needs structural control; ordinary edge counting alone is insufficient.

Uniform normalized loneliness time for every positive speed set contains the lonely-runner existence issue. Primary survey Conjecture 28 gives n<=5 only and discusses a conditional finite-reduction route; that does not provide a full proof.

Primary survey Conjecture 29 matches the structured denominator exactly. An executed exact interval calculation tested 1585 distinct speed sets of sizes 1..5 from 1..12, with zero grid misses and 29 singleton-only cases. This neither resolves all n nor handles general tight isolated times; no new hypothesis brief is justified.

The equality R(5,5)=43 requires excluding every 43-vertex Ramsey coloring or supplying a larger lower-bound witness to refute it. No candidate coloring or tractable complete exclusion certificate is available; no large SAT enumeration attempted.
